chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Khakan al-Dahqan, from Abu Sulaiman Dawud ibn Ghassan al-Bahrani, who said: I read to Abu Sahl Ismail ibn Ali al-Nuubakhti

The birth of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida ibn Musa ibn Ja'far al-Sadiq ibn Muhammad al-Baqir ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah's prayers be upon them all. He (peace be upon him) was born in Samarra in the year 256 AH. His mother was Saiqal, and he was known as Abu al-Qasim. By this kunya the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) testified, saying: His name is like my name, his kunya is like my kunya. His title is al-Mahdi, he is the Proof, he is the Awaited, and he is the Master of the Age (peace be upon him).

Ismail ibn Ali said: I entered upon Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) during the illness in which he died, while I was with him. He said to his servant Aqeed—who was a black Nubian who had served before him Ali ibn Muhammad and was the foster-son of al-Hasan (peace be upon him)—saying to him: 'O Aqeed, boil for me some water with mastic.' So he boiled it for him, then Saiqal, the maid, mother of the Caliph (peace be upon him), brought it to him. When the cup was in his hands and he was about to drink, his hand began to tremble so much that the cup struck the teeth of al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He let it go from his hand and said to Aqeed: 'Enter the house, for you will see a boy in prostration; bring him to me.'

Abu Sahl said: Aqeed said: I entered to look for him, and behold, I saw a boy in prostration raising his index finger towards the sky. I saluted him, and he shortened his prayer. I said: 'Indeed your master commands you to come out to him.' When his mother Saiqal came, she took his hand and brought him out to his father al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

Abu Sahl said: When the boy stood before him, he saluted, and behold, he was of a pearly complexion, with short hair on his head, and wide-set teeth. When al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw him, he wept and said: 'O master of my family, give me the water, for I am going to my Lord.' The boy took the boiled cup of mastic water in his hand, then moved his lips, and gave it to him to drink. When he had drunk it, he said: 'Prepare me for prayer.'

He placed a towel in his lap, and the boy performed ablution for him one part at a time, and wiped over his head and his feet. Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Give glad tidings, O my son, for you are the Master of the Age, you are the Mahdi, and you are the Proof of Allah on His earth. You are my son and my successor, and I gave birth to you, and you are Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave you birth, and you are the seal of the Pure Imams. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave glad tidings of you, named you, and gave you your kunya. By this my father testified to me from your pure forefathers. May Allah's prayers be upon the People of the House. Our Lord, indeed He is Praiseworthy and Glorious. And al-Hasan ibn Ali died at that very moment, may Allah's prayers be upon them all.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: Abu al-Qasim, the kunya (patronymic) of Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيّ: Al-Mahdi, the title meaning 'The Guided One'
key_terms.خَاتَمُ الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: Khatam al-Awsiya, the Seal of the Successors/Imams
key_terms.دَرِيُّ اللَّوْنِ: Dariy al-Lawn, having a pearly or luminous complexion
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الزَّمَانِ: Sahib al-Zaman, Master of the Age
key_terms.صَقِيلٌ: Saiqal, the mother of Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.مُصْطَكِيّ: Mastic, a resin used for flavoring water

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of Imam al-Mahdi's childhood as described in the hadith of his father's deathbed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a foundational narrative for the doctrine of the Minor and Major Ghaiba, detailing the birth of Imam al-Mahdi in Samarra and his immediate recognition by his father, Imam Hasan al-Askari. The account highlights the continuity of prophetic lineage through the 'detailed' genealogy and the miraculous signs of childhood, such as the trembling hand and the child's ability to perform ablution, which confirm his status as the awaited Hujjah. It serves as a key textual evidence for the Shia belief in the Imam's occultation and his role as the ultimate proof of God on earth.
